views.caveat: The list is one row per patient of each cohort; event counts and days come from the study's timeline, in days from diagnosis as the study records them. 5,368 patients. Sorted by Events (highest first), missing values last, across the cohort; every page is a slice of that one order, and the download holds every row kept, with every column.

steps.title: Count the patients per cohort and study
steps.detail: The timeline:counts query above: every patient of each cohort, with their sample count and, from the study's timeline, the number of events, the first and last event day (a range counted to its stop) and the event types — a patient with no timeline is listed with none.

steps.title: Sort them together and take one page
steps.detail: The timeline:rows query above: the patients of every cohort and study combined in one query, sorted by Events descending with missing values last, then patient id, and the 25 rows of the first page taken. Every other page, and the download, is the same query at another offset.

steps.title: Read P-0000012's timeline
steps.detail: The timeline:events and timeline:samples queries above: every clinical event recorded for P-0000012 in msk_chord_2024 with all its attributes, and the patient's samples with their SAMPLE_TYPE. Events are drawn as stored, in days from diagnosis; tracks group them by event type (case-folded) and nest them by attribute as cBioPortal's patient view does.

method.verification: A listing and one patient's record: no statistic is computed, so there is no script — the queries are the numbers.

views.caveat: P-0000012 — Mutations: 31 rows; Copy Number Alterations: 3 rows; Structural Variants: 0 rows. Each table lists a variant, a gene's call or an event once however many of the patient's samples carry it (Samples names them); allele frequency and read counts are the highest among those samples. Copy number is the deep calls only (AMP, HOMDEL), as the portal's patient view lists them; Copy # on a mutation is the gene's deep calls anywhere in the patient. Cohort % is the share of the study's samples profiled for the gene by their panel with a mutation in it, or with the same copy-number call. Annotation is OncoKB v7.5 (oncogenicity and its highest sensitivity level); structural variants carry the study's own annotation, not OncoKB's. The patient list: 5,368 patients. Sorted with patients who have any alteration first, then by patient id across the cohort; every page is a slice of that one order, and the download holds every row kept, with every column.

steps.title: Count the patients per cohort and study
steps.detail: The alterations:counts query above: every patient of each cohort, with the count of the patient's samples and how many rows each of the three tables lists for them over those samples (a mutation, a gene's deep copy-number call, a structural variant — each counted once however many samples carry it).

steps.title: Sort them together and take one page
steps.detail: The alterations:rows query above: the patients of every cohort and study combined in one query, sorted patients with any alteration first, then by patient id, and the 25 rows of the first page taken. Every other page, and the download, is the same query at another offset.

steps.title: Read P-0000012's three tables
steps.detail: The alterations:mutations, alterations:cna and alterations:sv queries above, each paged, searched, filtered and sorted in the database like any table view. Each table reads the patient's samples. Mutations: every called mutation of those samples (uncalled calls left out), one row per variant with the samples carrying it, the highest allele frequency among them (variant / (variant + reference) reads) with that sample's reads, and the gene's deep copy-number calls in those samples (Copy #). Copy-number alterations: the deep calls (AMP, HOMDEL), one row per gene and call. Structural variants: one row per event (both genes and breakpoints, class, event info), the highest read counts among its samples. Cohort % is the share of the study's samples profiled for the gene (by their gene panel) with any mutation in it, or with the same copy-number call; the annotation is the OncoKB v7.5 call for the protein change, or for AMPLIFICATION / DELETION.

method.verification: A listing: no statistic is computed, so there is no script — the queries are the numbers.
